Build a Random-Forest Learner Adapter (Calibrated, Scoped)

Source: R/learner_rf.R
make_ranger_adapter.Rd

Returns a closure that fits ONE ranger random forest on a single bootstrap subsample and returns a logical selection mask over the features, mirroring the role of make_glmnet_adapter() for tree-based learners.

Usage

make_ranger_adapter(num_trees = 500L, family = "gaussian")

Arguments

num_trees

Positive integer; number of trees per forest (ranger's num.trees). Default 500L.

family

Character scalar; response family passed to the batch adapter. Default "gaussian".

Value

A function with signature function(x, y, lambda_val) -> logical vector of length ncol(x) for use inside stabl_fit(), where lambda_val is a 1-row data.frame from the threshold grid (see auto_rf_threshold_grid()).

Details

This adapter factory is primarily an internal backend used by stabl_fit() (base_learner = "rf"). The response family is inferred by ranger from y (numeric -> regression, factor -> classification, Surv -> survival); stabl_fit() coerces y for the binomial/multinomial families. The forest seed is drawn from the caller's RNG stream so that results are reproducible under stabl_fit()'s random_state and identical across sequential and parallel execution.

Selection rule

Instead of a penalty path, the RF adapter sweeps an importance-threshold path. The grid (see auto_rf_threshold_grid()) contains quantiles of the pooled permutation-importance distribution; given a 1-row grid lambda_val, a feature is selected when its permutation importance is >= the row's threshold. Lower thresholds therefore give supersets of the selections at higher thresholds — the same sparse-to-dense nesting the glmnet lambda path provides, so the stability-accumulation and FDP+ logic in stabl_fit() work unchanged.

Statistical guardrails (read before using)

  • Permutation importance, not Gini. Gini importance is biased towards high-cardinality features; permutation importance is the better-studied choice for null calibration (Boruta likewise builds on mean-decrease-accuracy).

  • Pair with model-X knockoff artificial features. A random forest is a multivariate learner: real null features correlated with true signals receive leaked importance, and permuted null features (artificial_type = "random_permutation") do not reproduce that leakage, so the FDP+ estimate is anti-conservative. Model-X knockoff nulls ("knockoff_equi" / "knockoff_mvr") preserve the correlation structure and are the only statistically sound pairing. Combining base_learner = "rf" with artificial_type = "random_permutation" in stabl_fit() emits a package warning to this effect.

  • Calibrated within a measured scope (WS-2). With knockoff_equi decoys the mean empirical FDP is 0.025 (linear design) and 0.065 (low-dimensional nonlinear design), meeting the predeclared criterion; it is NOT met at p = 50 with strong correlation (0.44) or for binary outcomes (0.26). Simulation evidence, not a guarantee.

See also

auto_rf_threshold_grid(), make_glmnet_adapter(), stabl_fit()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1L)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(200L), 20L, 10L,
              dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("f", 1:10)))
  y <- x[, 1] * x[, 2] + rnorm(20L)
  grid  <- stablr:::auto_rf_threshold_grid(x, y, n_grid = 5L,
                                           num_trees = 100L, seed = 1L)
  adapter <- stablr:::make_ranger_adapter(num_trees = 100L)
  mask <- adapter(x, y, grid[1L, , drop = FALSE])
  cat("selected at sparsest threshold:", sum(mask), "of", ncol(x), "\n")
}
#> selected at sparsest threshold: 0 of 10
